clue.text: A little relic apt to be damaged

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone worries that a small old relic might easily get broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be damaged' rearranges RELIC and APT. 'A little' looks like it describes the relic but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a tiny bit or speck of something, a small amount.

clue.text: Left with a pound to make an entree

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
L stands for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Money and directions to get into somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entree' means a way in, not a main course.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is an entrance, and a grand doorway or gate is one.

clue.text: Salad food for an artist?

parts.note: an artist is an RA, a Royal Academician, and his plate of food is his dish

explanation.surface: Asking what a painter might eat in a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword staple for artist, and a dish is food.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp red root vegetable eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: At home, so main problem may be staying awake

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: a problem jumbles things up, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Being home is no help when sleeplessness is the trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges SO MAIN after IN (at home).
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeplessness is the condition of being unable to fall asleep.

clue.text: See move as a firm sign

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or look
go means move

explanation.surface: A chess player watches a move as a sure signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' is a company, not something solid.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's emblem or trademark symbol.

clue.text: Fish left-one caught a pungent odour from it!

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An angler's catch gives off a strong smell.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the bulb that gives off the smell, read cryptically: something known for a pungent odour.
explanation.definitionFit: This bulb is famous for its strong smell, which lingers on the breath after eating it.

clue.text: Takes up commercial post with organisation

parts.note: an ad is a commercial

indicators.note: organisation means putting into a new order, so the letters of post are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone accepts a job advertised by a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' rearranges POST into OPTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To take up a child or an idea as your own.

clue.text: Dog the French supporter-stick around

parts.note: la is French for the
a bra is a supporting garment

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word for stick is read backwards

parts.note: a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: A French dog with a lead and stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' is a garment, not a fan; 'around' turns the stick backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of retriever dog.

clue.text: I am as the northern star',declared Julius Caesar

definitions.text: I am as the northern star',declared Julius Caesar

parts.words: I am as the northern star',declared Julius Caesar
parts.note: Shakespeare's Caesar boasts he is as unmoving as the pole star; the missing word in the quote is the answer

explanation.surface: A line from Shakespeare's play about Julius Caesar.
explanation.walkthrough: The quote in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar is 'I am constant as the northern star': the missing word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unchanging and steadfast, like the pole star that never moves in the sky.

clue.text: Work out, not for the first time

definitions.text: Work out, not for the first time

parts.words: Work out, not for the first time
parts.note: to work out a plan is to design it; doing it again, not for the first time, is designing it once more

explanation.surface: Someone does a workout but has done it before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' suggests exercise, but it means devise a plan; doing that again is the sense needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To plan something anew is to devise it again in a different form.

clue.text: Turning heads, being sweet

indicators.note: turning round means the slang words for heads are read backwards here

parts.note: a nob is slang for the head, so two heads give nob twice

explanation.surface: A pleasant person makes heads turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' reverses NOBNOB (two NOBs, slang for heads).
explanation.definitionFit: A bonbon is a small confection, a piece of candy.

clue.text: Suggest the fellow should be told to go elsewhere

parts.note: to move a motion is to suggest it formally
a don is a fellow of a college

explanation.surface: Proposing that a man be sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a university fellow; 'should be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Police tell loiterers to shift along, sending them away from where they stand.

clue.text: Think playing tricks amuses?

indicators.note: letters that play tricks change places, so the word amuses is rearranged

explanation.surface: A joker wonders whether pranks are entertaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing tricks' rearranges AMUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume is to suppose or take for granted, a way of thinking.

clue.text: An arrangement to make a reduction

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a binding agreement; the verb means to shrink or tighten up.

clue.text: A woman's name for lip lines?

parts.note: marge is an old word for margin, a lip or edge
RY is short for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A name for the creases around the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: RY is the crossword abbreviation for railway (lines).
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional English female given name.

clue.text: He'll blow up over 500 eventually

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals; the wordplay needs DI, which is 501
eventually means later on

explanation.surface: Someone will lose their temper about a large sum before long.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay needs DI, Roman 501, so the printed 500 is a slip (or a lost 1). 'over' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that dilates widens or expands, so one who does this enlarges things.

clue.text: Silly Billy the diver

definitions.meaning: a foolish person, a crazy one
a diving waterbird, called a diver in Britain

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a crazy person and is also the North American name for the diving bird.

clue.text: Container crates in bad state

indicators.note: in a bad state means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A box found among damaged crates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad state' rearranges CRATES IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cylindrical tin or box for storing things.

clue.text: Brave children

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior, so his little ones are meant, not courageous kids

explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective but is a noun, a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: Native American babies, especially carried on the back.

clue.text: Taking some photographs and thereby causing a split

definitions.meaning: taking quick photos, as with a camera

explanation.definitionFit: The word means taking snapshots and also breaking with a crack.

clue.text: Some soberly-clad ambitious man

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A quietly dressed but ambitious fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' finds the run ending soberly-clAD AMbitious.
explanation.definitionFit: The first man in the Bible, whose name stands for any male.

clue.text: There's possibly no guard on the beach

indicators.note: possibly means the letters might be arranged another way, so they are shuffled here

explanation.surface: A beach without a lifeguard on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges NO GUARD. 'on the beach' is a ship stuck on shore, not a sunbather.
explanation.definitionFit: A stranded ship has run up on the shore and is stuck there.

clue.text: Leftwinger's internal discomfort

indicators.note: internal says the answer is found inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A left-wing politician feels uneasy inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internal' finds the run inside lefTWINGEr's.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden sharp pang of pain.

clue.text: A feast makes serving men late

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, men serving in the army
past means late, gone by

explanation.surface: Soldiers arrive after the banquet has begun.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps. 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A meal, especially a substantial one.

clue.text: A heavenly body from remote parts

indicators.note: parts here means split up, so the letters of remote are separated and rearranged

explanation.surface: A star seen from distant places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' rearranges REMOTE; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star, a space rock burning up in the sky.

clue.text: Pressing for decorative use of metal?

definitions.text: Pressing for decorative use of metal?

parts.words: Pressing for decorative use of metal?
parts.note: pressing clothes with a hot flat appliance is a domestic job; the same name for metal plus the word for a job gives ornamental metal goods

explanation.surface: Asking whether metal is pressed for ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: Pressing is ironing, a chore; read as two words, the chore's name also describes ornamental metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental gates, railings and grilles made of wrought metal.

clue.text: Each one houses a bird

indicators.note: houses means the word for one holds the bird inside it

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
pie is an old name for the magpie

explanation.surface: Every single home has a bird in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Pie is an old name for the magpie, and the ace is the one in cards; 'houses' sets the bird within.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means for every one, as in 'a pound per item'.

clue.text: Finding nothing right, almost everyone is vocal

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the word for everyone is dropped

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: Most people say something unanimously when nothing is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken rather than written, by mouth.

clue.text: It's an Oriental health-drink prepared from herbs

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: An Eastern herbal tonic made up for health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' sits after its fodder and reworks the first two words into TISAN; E (east, for Oriental) follows. 'from herbs' describes the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An infusion of herbs taken as a soothing, healthy brew.

clue.text: Getting rid of unwanted moisture, takes a reading

indicators.note: takes here signals that the letters of the phrase are taken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Draining off excess water needs a measurement first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' rearranges A READING.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing excess water through pipes or ditches.

clue.text: Charges for some plants

definitions.meaning: tall grass-like plants growing by water

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means dashes headlong; the noun is the marsh plants used for matting.

clue.text: A wretch who's second-rate-of less consequence

parts.note: B is second grade, after A
lighter means less weighty or important

explanation.surface: A wretched person is inferior and unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: B is the grade below A, so second-rate. 'who's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal word for a contemptible or annoying person, a rascal.
